title: EP-Flow: Disordered Crystal Structure Prediction without Site-Level Annotations
authors: Qiuliang Liu, Liming Wu, Qi Li, Zhonglong Peng, Chang Chen, Xiaolong Chen, Wenbing Huang, Shifeng Jin
abstract: Generative models have made rapid progress in ordered crystal structure prediction, yet many functional materials are intrinsically disordered, with substitutional mixing, vacancies, or interstitial species controlling their properties. Existing crystal generators either assume deterministic site occupations or require site-level disorder annotations, which are often unavailable when the chemical formula is the primary input. We formulate disordered crystal structure prediction through an Occupancy Distribution Matrix (ODM), a continuous site-by-species representation that unifies ordered crystals, solid solutions, vacancy disorder, and interstitial occupancy. A valid ODM must satisfy coupled site-wise occupancy, mass-conservation, and non-negativity constraints, placing each sample on a formula-dependent transportation polytope. We propose Entropic Polytope Flow (EP-Flow), a marginal-constrained flow matching framework that canonicalizes heterogeneous polytopes into a shared double-centered space, learns a marginal-preserving flow, and recovers feasible occupancies through a Sinkhorn inverse map. By jointly generating occupancies, fractional coordinates, and lattice parameters, EP-Flow achieves state-of-the-art performance on formula-conditioned disordered CSP benchmarks derived from COD and MPDS, substantially outperforming adapted ordered-crystal generators. Analyses further show that EP-Flow recovers sparse and chemically meaningful local disorder patterns rather than merely matching global composition statistics.
summary: This paper introduces EP-Flow, a novel generative model for predicting disordered crystal structures directly from a chemical formula. It reformulates the problem using an Occupancy Distribution Matrix (ODM) constrained by a transportation polytope. By mapping this complex geometry into a shared latent space and using flow matching, EP-Flow accurately predicts both the site occupancies and the underlying crystal structure, outperforming existing methods.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of predicting crystal structures for intrinsically disordered materials without requiring explicit, site-level annotations of the disorder.
main_result: EP-Flow achieves state-of-the-art performance on disordered CSP benchmarks by learning a flow that respects the complex constraints of the chemical formula.
method: It employs an Occupancy Distribution Matrix (ODM) formulation, canonicalizes the resulting polytope into a shared latent space, and uses a marginal-constrained flow matching framework.
model_or_system: The system is a crystalline solid exhibiting disorder (substitutional mixing, vacancies), modeled by an ODM that must satisfy coupled site-wise occupancy and mass-conservation constraints, defining a transportation polytope.
key_observables: Match Rate, Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD), Occupancy Mean Absolute Error (OccMAE), and the Occupancy Distribution Matrix (ODM).
important_parameters: The model jointly generates occupancies, fractional coordinates, and lattice parameters; the process relies on Sinkhorn projection for constraint enforcement.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the problem can be mapped to a continuous flow matching framework by canonicalizing the heterogeneous polytope into a shared, double-centered space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal representation $(A, F, l)$, the canonicalization of the polytope via log-domain double centering, and the joint flow generation process, alongside structural reconstruction trajectories.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the problem using the ODM and its associated transportation polytope. It then introduces EP-Flow, detailing the canonicalization to a shared latent space, the flow learning mechanism, and the final recovery via Sinkhorn projection for joint generation of occupancies, coordinates, and lattice parameters.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science, the use of flow matching to enforce complex, high-dimensional geometric and physical constraints (like mass conservation) within a generative model framework is highly relevant to modeling quantum many-body states or complex quantum field configurations.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Overview of EP-Flow for disordered crystal generation. (a) Disordered crystal represented by (A, F , l). (b) Occupancy matrix canonicalized from formula polytope P(1N, c) to double-centered space M0(N, M) via log-domain double centering, which recovers back by Sinkhorn projection. (c) Joint flow matching over (A′, F , l) conditioned on c, with projection back to A for the final structure.

Figure 3: Reconstruction results for disordered functional materials. Each row compares predicted vs. ground-truth structures, with RMSD and OccMAE. Key-site occupancies are annotated; the rightmost column shows the site with largest occupancy error. Three disorder types are covered: oxygen-vacancy, interstitial/partial-occupancy, and mixed-cation/anion substitutional.
